title: What is the Electoral College?
body: When citizens vote for President, they choose electors pledged to candidates. Electors meet to cast official votes.
context: The Constitution (Article II, amended by the 12th) created the system; Congress sets the timeline for counting electoral votes.

title: 538 electors
body: There are 538 electoral votes total — 435 House + 100 Senate + 3 for Washington, D.C.
prompt: How many electoral votes are there in total?
context: The number changes only if House seat apportionment or D.C. status changes.

title: 270 to win
body: A candidate needs a majority of electoral votes — at least 270 — to become President.
prompt: How many electoral votes does a presidential candidate need to win?
context: If no candidate reaches 270, the House decides the President (12th Amendment procedure).

title: Popular vote vs electoral vote
body: The national popular vote total does not decide the presidency — electoral votes do, state by state (mostly winner-take-all).
context: Five elections (including 2000 and 2016) saw a president elected without winning the national popular vote.

title: When electors meet
body: Electors meet in their states in December after the November general election; Congress counts votes in January.
context: The President is inaugurated on January 20.
